claims.claim: Finite-horizon play is exactly represented by a perfect-recall belief-state recurrence.
claims.evidence: For fixed White king/queen squares, every hidden Black square gives the same legal-move observation, while every attacked Black square is individually visible. After a White move, these are exactly the block S\A and singleton blocks {b} for b in S∩A. Legal adjacent Black replies then partition by the next observation, with king capture losing for White, protected-queen capture or movement into White's attack set winning on White's next move, and all remaining unseen destinations unioned into the successor belief. Induction on the remaining White-move horizon proves the existential-White/universal-Black recurrence. The checker exhaustively confirmed this observation equivalence for 249,984 concrete placements and 15,499,008 ordered pairs of possible Black squares. It also checked all 23,520 king-only evasion cases supporting the treatment of an unprotected queen capture as non-winning for White.
claims.search_method: Direct finite-horizon induction, supplemented by exhaustive integer/bitset checks of observation equivalence, transition geometry, and the king-only evasion invariant.

claims.claim: With draw termination suppressed, the exact worst-case capture time over all initial configurations is 23 White moves.
claims.evidence: Independent exhaustive belief-state dynamic programming enumerated all 64·63·62=249,984 labeled placements. The numbers whose minimum capture horizons are 1 through 23 were exactly [105476,12080,13412,18928,13776,14464,7656,4484,6176,8664,11804,7492,3416,2140,5396,6108,3428,1524,1984,1212,196,136,32]. Thus every placement is winning within 23, while 32 are not winning within 22, establishing both bounds.
claims.witness: The 32 sharp placements are represented by WK=a1, BK=d4 and WQ=b1, h2, g5, or h7, together with their eight board symmetries.
claims.search_method: Exact uint64 belief-set AND/OR dynamic programming over every legal White move, observation block, and adjacent Black reply; all eight board symmetries were checked and canonicalized. No floating point was used.

claims.claim: Even with the source’s host-enforced repetition rule, White can guarantee capture within 28 White moves.
claims.evidence: The independent history-augmented AND/OR search succeeded for all 18,081 symmetry classes covering all 144,508 initially invisible placements; the other 105,476 placements are captured on move 1. Each class was solved within its draw-suppressed optimum plus five White moves, with maximum budget 28. The augmented state records exact multiplicities of ordered White king/queen square-pairs and disallows a third occurrence. Any threefold repetition of a complete position would require its White-piece pair to occur at least three times, so these policies preclude the host repetition draw. Capture by White's 28th move also precedes the fifty-move limit.
claims.witness: The exhaustive run returned repetition_safe_classes_succeeded=18081 of 18081 and maximum_white_move_budget=28 after 4,396,529 history-solver calls.
claims.search_method: Exact history-dependent belief-state search using collision-checked sparse pair multisets and joint board/history canonicalization under all eight symmetries. No floating point was used.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether White can guarantee capture within 50 White moves from every source-legal initial configuration under the source draw rules. Claim 2 establishes the stronger uniform bound of 28 while structurally preventing threefold repetition; the exhaustive enumeration covers every distinct placement. Therefore the draft's affirmative final answer and FULL claimed_resolution are accurate. The separate exact value 23 applies only when draw termination is suppressed, as the draft states.
